q: The Algorithmic Sufficient Statistic of a string x is a set S ∋ x (a hypothesis) such that:
opts: S has minimum description length K(S)
K(x) = K(S) + log|S| + O(log n) — the two-part description S (model) then x's rank in S is as short as any description
exp: Algorithmic sufficient statistic: S is sufficient for x if K(x|S) ≈ log|S| (random within S) and K(S) + log|S| ≈ K(x) (S captures all meaningful structure). This formalises the distinction between random and structural components of x.
